title.narrative: Output 4.3. Increased capacity of Member States to develop policies, legislation and other measures that are specifically aimed at facilitating the transition of enterprises to formality

description.narrative: 1.The Government of Zimbabwe has developed an Action Plan to operationalise a National Strategy on Formalization: a. The Action Plan was adopted after national wide tripartite+ consultations and aims to facilitate the transition to formality of enterprises and the workers they employ. 2. The Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions-through its affiliate the Zimbabwe Chamber of Informal Economy Associations has developed and is offering improved services to informal enterprises or own-account workers in Bulawayo in view to facilitating their transition to formality: a. 104 operators and their associations were sensitised on Recommendation 204, opportunities for digitalising their businesses and to engage in the national formalisation agenda with other key stakeholders including local and national government departments. b. 70 entrepreneurs received Business Development Service Training using the Improve Your Business (IYB) training to include innovation and registering their companies to enable them to supply to local authorities and government. c.70 enterprises employing over 200 workers have accessed refurbished OSH compliant workspaces under a Pilot Initiative with the Bulawayo City Council in partnership with a local private property management company-Old Mutual Zimbabwe, academia- National University of Science and Technology (NUST) and the Bulawayo SMEs Trust. 3. Based on a rapid assessment of the impacts of the covid-19 pandemic on informal economy workers, the Bulawayo Chambers of SMEs supported their membership to access their workspaces during lockdown restrictive measures. a. The Bulawayo Chambers of SMEs sought authorisation from the Government to issue informal business operators and workers travelling passes to move between their residencies, workspaces, and to and from markets as well to access service providers. b. Twelve (12) enterprises were registered and repurposed their businesses to respond to covid-19 and manufacture covid-19 PPEs. 1. Through Regular Budget Supplementary Account (RBSA), Regular Budget Technical Cooperation (RBTC) and the UN Multi-Partner Trust Fund (MPTF) for COVID-19 Response and Recovery Programme the ILO provided both financial and technical support towards the drafting, the public dialogue and consultations and the national validation of the action plan, including: a. A multistakeholder knowledge sharing workshop featuring efforts on enterprise formalization in Zimbabwe as well as best practices from across Africa. 2. The ILO provided training on OSH protocols in line with the national response plan, sensitised key stakeholders, and enterprises on R204 and facilitated the PPP dialogue with local authorities and the private sector. 3. The ILO supported the registration of selected SMEs with the Ministry of Women Affairs, Community, Small and Medium Enterprises Development and the design and dissemination of information, education, and communication materials to showcase various enterprise formalization pathways and the opportunities for SMEs in the Covid-19 response.

description.narrative: The National Policy on OSH has been reviewed and is being operationalized through a stakeholders’ consultative process. Strategies implemented thus far include the enhancement of constituents’ OSH capacity and awareness raising, development of sector-specific guidance and tools for management of OSH risks, including OSH management systems for informal economy and formulation of the new harmonised OSH legislation (adoption of the legislation to be confirmed). The successful implementation of the national OSH policy will benefit the national competent authorities including the inspectorates, employers and workers representatives through reinforced mandates and enhanced capacities, as well as the workers and enterprises including workers in informal sector, and other workers in situations of vulnerability, through extended protection and reduction of occupational injuries and diseases. The ILO provided technical support towards the build-up activities that led to the review and commencement of the implementation of the National OSH Policy, including: a. Introduction of the inspectors, business leaders and members of the employers organizations to the concept of OSH as a Fundamental Principle and Rights at Work (FPRW) in order to improve the quality of inspections and to enhance the quality of negotiation for and consideration of OSH rights. b. Sensitization of the employers, workers and OSH stakeholders to C190 from an OSH perspective to enhance the integration of psychological hazards, including violence and harassment, into the OSH management systems and risk management. c. specific guidelines, tools and materials on OSH and FPRW and C190.
